assessments.technical_explanation: This advisory matches a dependency declared in the lockfile for a RisuAI browser plugin built with Vite. The project ships a single bundled JS file; build-time dev dependencies are not included in the runtime output. The production dependencies are limited to localforage, svelte, lucide-svelte, and a queue data structure, none of which are typical targets for this advisory class. The advisory most likely affects a dev-only tool such as Vite or PostCSS, whose vulnerable code paths involve development servers or build-time processing that do not execute when the built plugin runs inside RisuAI.
assessments.layman_explanation: A build tool used during development has a known security issue, but that tool is not part of the finished plugin that users install. The risk to end users is minimal.
assessments.developer_action: Update the affected dev dependency to a patched version during the next build cycle.

observations.title: All flagged advisories map to build-time tooling with no runtime reachability in the shipped bundle
observations.technical_explanation: The root package declares only four runtime dependencies, while the remaining dependencies are devDependencies used for bundling, transpilation, minification, and styling. The build script produces a single dist JS file that RisuAI imports as a plugin; node_modules and build tooling are not shipped. The OSV advisories correspond to development/build packages whose vulnerable code paths (dev servers, build-time input processing, or compiler internals) are not present or reachable in the runtime artifact, and whose triggering inputs are not attacker-controlled in this project's build workflow.
observations.layman_explanation: Every warning here is about tools used to create the plugin, not the plugin file that users actually load. Because those tools are left out of the finished plugin, none of these warnings reach people using the extension.
observations.developer_action: Run a routine dependency update to clear the advisories from scanner output; this is hygiene rather than an urgent security fix for users.

observations.title: Advisory identification limited by truncated lock file context
observations.technical_explanation: The supplied source context shows only the first 41 lines of a 100KB file, covering the root package declaration but not the full transitive dependency tree. Scanner explanations had package details removed. Assessments are based on the project structure: a Vite-built browser plugin with minimal production dependencies (queue, localforage, lucide-svelte, svelte) and standard build devDependencies. Most flagged advisories in this dependency profile correspond to build-time tools that do not ship in the bundled artifact. If any advisory actually targets a production dependency with runtime-reachable vulnerable code, the impact could be higher. A full lock file review would improve confidence.
observations.layman_explanation: The security scanner found several known issues in dependencies, but only a small portion of the dependency list was provided for review. Based on the project structure, most of these issues appear to be in building tools that do not end up in the final plugin. Providing the full dependency list would allow a more precise review.
observations.developer_action: Run npm audit with the full lock file to identify each flagged package, update all dependencies to patched versions, and verify that production dependencies specifically are current.

limitations: This advisory review cannot prove the absence of unknown behavior.
